verses.english: “Mendicants, I will teach you a duality.

verses.pali: Cakkhuñceva rūpā ca, sotañceva saddā ca, ghānañceva gandhā ca, jivhā ceva rasā ca, kāyo ceva phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ceva dhammā ca—
verses.english: It’s just the eye and sights, the ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and touches, and the mind and ideas.
Mendicants, suppose someone was to say:

verses.pali: ‘ahametaṁ dvayaṁ paccakkhāya aññaṁ dvayaṁ paññapessāmī’ti, tassa vācāvatthukamevassa.
verses.english: ‘I’ll deny this duality and describe another duality.’ They’d have no grounds for that claim,
they’d be stumped by questions, and, in addition, they’d get frustrated.
Because they’re out of their element.”
